A refund has three statuses. In `requested`, the request was recorded and is still waiting for a decision. In `paid`, the amount was returned to the customer and there is a payment date. [policy:refund-policy#refund-statuses]. Rejection reasons [policy:refund-policy#rejection-reasons]. The rejection reason is kept on the refund itself. A rejection for the window is automatic and needs no review, but the analyst must check the capture date and the merchant's window before explaining the decision to the customer. Chargeback fee [policy:fees-and-pricing#chargeback-fee]. Chargeback fee [policy:chargeback-handling#fee-reference]. Each dispute opened creates a fixed fee charged to the merchant, even if the merchant wins the defense. The fee amount and the rule for charging it per period are in the fees and pricing policy. The fee is deducted in the settlement of the period in which the dispute was opened. [policy:chargeback-handling#fee-reference]. Fee currency [policy:fees-and-pricing#fee-currency]. Fees are charged in the merchant's settlement currency. The fixed chargeback fee is 15.00 in that currency, with no conversion: a merchant that settles in Brazilian reais pays 15.00 reais, and one that settles in euros pays 15.00 euros. Payments in another currency do not count in the gross volume and so do not generate the weekly processing fee. [policy:fees-and-pricing#fee-currency]. Questions about fees [policy:fees-and-pricing#fee-questions]. When the merchant asks why the payout was lower than the sales, the answer separates three deductions: refunds paid in the week, the 2.9% processing fee on the gross volume and the fixed fee per chargeback opened. Each deduction is shown as a number, computed with the calculation tool, and nothing is estimated. [policy:fees-and-pricing#fee-questions].

Duplicate charges [policy:refund-policy#duplicate-exception]. Failures and retries [policy:duplicate-charges#retries-after-failure]. A declined attempt followed by an approved attempt is not a duplicate, because only the second payment was captured. The detection rule considers only captured payments. The analyst must ignore attempts with a failed status when looking for duplicates. [policy:duplicate-charges#retries-after-failure]. Overview [policy:duplicate-charges#overview]. A duplicate charge happens when the same payment is captured twice by mistake, for example because the customer clicked pay twice or because the merchant sent it again. This policy defines how to recognize a duplicate and how to return the amount to the customer. [policy:duplicate-charges#overview]. Detection rule [policy:duplicate-charges#detection-rule].

Overview [policy:fx-reference-rates#overview]. The reference exchange rate is the market value used to compare with the rate the merchant applied in a conversion. This policy says which source to use, how to handle weekends and holidays and what to do when the rate is not available. [policy:fx-reference-rates#overview]. Official source [policy:fx-reference-rates#source]. Records [policy:cross-currency-refunds#records]. For each cross-currency refund the system keeps the requested currency and amount, the paid currency and amount, the applied rate, the rate date and the conversion identifier. The reference rate is not kept on the refund record: it is looked up from the official source at analysis time, and the source and date used go into the answer's evidence. [policy:cross-currency-refunds#records]. Currency with no rate [policy:fx-reference-rates#unsupported-currency-handling]. When the currency has no reference rate, the analyst must not make up an estimate or use another source without saying so. The answer says the reference rate does not exist for that currency, states what prevents the comparison and points to what would resolve the case, for example an official source for that currency. The case goes to human review. [policy:fx-reference-rates#unsupported-currency-handling].

Merchant markup [policy:cross-currency-refunds#merchant-fx-markup]. Merchants on the `markup` plan can apply up to 3.0% below the reference rate when converting a refund. The markup lowers the applied rate: the applied rate is the reference rate on the refund date multiplied by one minus the markup. The markup must be in the merchant's settlement terms, and a markup above the limit must be taken to human review. [policy:cross-currency-refunds#merchant-fx-markup]. Merchants on the standard plan [policy:cross-currency-refunds#standard-plan]. Merchants on the `standard` plan apply no markup. For them, the rate applied to the refund is the reference rate on the refund date itself. If the analyst finds a difference larger than rounding for a merchant on the standard plan, the difference is not a markup and the case must be investigated and, if needed, escalated. [policy:cross-currency-refunds#standard-plan]. Overview [policy:fx-reference-rates#overview]. The reference exchange rate is the market value used to compare with the rate the merchant applied in a conversion. This policy says which source to use, how to handle weekends and holidays and what to do when the rate is not available. [policy:fx-reference-rates#overview]. Worked example [policy:cross-currency-refunds#worked-example]. Take a payment of EUR 200.00 converted on the charge at 5.5000, which gives BRL 1,100.00. On the refund day the reference rate is 5.4000 and the merchant applies a 2.0% markup, so the applied rate is 5.2920 and the customer receives BRL 1,058.40. The difference is BRL 41.60: BRL 20.00 comes from the rate movement and BRL 21.60 comes from the markup. [policy:cross-currency-refunds#worked-example].

Evidence for not received [policy:chargeback-handling#evidence-nrc]. In a dispute for a product not received, the main evidence is the proof of delivery with a date and a signature, or the tracking code with the carrier's confirmation. For digital services, the record of the customer's access to the service serves as proof. The delivery time promised to the customer must also be attached. [policy:chargeback-handling#evidence-nrc]. Evidence for not as described [policy:chargeback-handling#evidence-nad]. In a dispute for a product different from the description, the merchant must show the description published at the time of purchase, photos of the product shipped and the exchange policy the customer accepted. If the customer already got a partial refund or an exchange, the proof must be attached, because it lowers the disputed amount. [policy:chargeback-handling#evidence-nad]. Overview [policy:chargeback-handling#overview]. A chargeback is a dispute the cardholder opens with the issuing bank to ask for a payment back. Acme Payments gets the notice of the dispute, informs the merchant and prepares the defense. This policy defines the stages, the deadlines and the evidence required. [policy:chargeback-handling#overview]. Evidence checklist [policy:chargeback-handling#evidence-checklist]. The evidence depends on the reason code. For `FRD`, attach the confirmation of the device, the delivery address and contact with the customer. For `NRC`, attach the proof of delivery or of access to the service. For `NAD`, attach the product description, the photos and the message exchange. For `DUP`, attach the proof that the two charges come from different orders. The reason code picks the list. [policy:chargeback-handling#evidence-checklist].

note: Real run of the two arms over the same set of cases, over the same ledger, with the same model and with the deterministic judge of the repository. One run per case: the numbers are a trend and not a statistical significance. The answer of the studio is composed and not written by a model: it renders the evidence the verifier supported, and a case the studio did not resolve counts in the denominator like any other. The dollars of a model whose price nobody verified are unknown, and unknown is never zero.

rule.decision: The studio is a gain only when it resolves strictly more cases than the single agent over the same 31 cases, with a difference of at least 2 cases, and its cost per resolved case is not higher than the cost per resolved case of the single agent. A difference of 0 or 1 case is a trend and not a gain. A studio that costs more and answers the same is not a gain. When the money of an arm is unknown, the comparison of the money is not established and the flag stays off. The flag stays off in every other case, and the result is published either way.

uncertainty: One run per case over 31 cases makes the difference of the arms a trend and not a statistical significance. The page of the result publishes the interval of the difference of the correctness, and an interval that covers zero keeps the flag off. The threshold of 2 cases is a decision of the repository and not a significance, and the page says so.
